about: What the FY2026 school general fund ledger at period 13 shows was left unspent, against the range the period-12 ledger allowed and what the School Committee was told in July 2026.

category_rules.label: Teachers & substitutes
category_rules.rule: salary lines, functions 2300–2399 except 2330 (teachers, special-education teachers, specialists, substitutes, librarians)

category_rules.label: Counselors & psychologists
category_rules.rule: salary lines, functions 2700–2899 (guidance, social workers, psychologists)

category_rules.label: Administrators & office staff
category_rules.rule: salary lines, functions 1000–2299 (central office, directors, principals, secretaries)

category_rules.label: Nurses, coaches & other staff
category_rules.rule: every other salary line (nurses, athletics, advisors, reserves)

category_rules.label: Out-of-district tuition
category_rules.rule: functions 9000 and up (private and collaborative special-education tuition)

category_rules.label: Special-ed contracted services
category_rules.rule: non-salary lines, functions 2310 and 2320 (contracted therapists, evaluations, tutoring)

category_rules.label: Transportation
category_rules.rule: non-salary lines, function 3300 (regular and special-education buses)

category_rules.label: Building & grounds upkeep
category_rules.rule: every other non-salary line in functions 4000–4999 (repairs, contracted maintenance, custodial and grounds supplies)

category_rules.label: Equipment & technology
category_rules.rule: functions 7000–7999, and 2451 (furniture, equipment, computers and their leases)

category_rules.label: Supplies, services & everything else
category_rules.rule: every remaining non-salary line (classroom supplies, textbooks, professional development, legal, dues, athletics expenses, office services)

benefits.causes: fewer employees enrolled in the health plan than budgeted, staff opting out, or premiums below the estimate
benefits.settles: health-plan enrolment by month and the premium rates

buildings.causes: maintenance projects postponed or not started, a shortage of facilities staff to run them, or a deliberate hold on spending
buildings.settles: the facilities work-order and project list with dates

counselors.causes: a counselor or psychologist post vacant or on leave for part of the year, or the work bought from a contractor instead
counselors.settles: the position-control roster by month for functions 2710 and 2800

other_staff.causes: stipends not paid for seasons or programs that did not run, or a nurse post vacant for part of the year
other_staff.settles: the stipend and nursing payroll by month

paras.causes: aides hired late or not at all, or aides paid from a grant instead
paras.settles: paraprofessional payroll by month and by funding source

sped_services.causes: more children needing contracted therapy or evaluation than budgeted, or contractors covering for vacant staff posts
sped_services.settles: the contracted-service invoices by service type

supplies.causes: a deliberate hold on purchasing, or purchases made from grants and revolving funds instead
supplies.settles: the general-fund journal detail by month

teachers.causes: a post left vacant or filled late, a leave of absence covered for less than the salary, or teachers hired at a lower step than budgeted
teachers.settles: the district’s position-control roster by month: each budgeted post, who held it, from when, and at what step

transport.causes: route or contract prices above budget, or special-education routes added mid-year
transport.settles: the transportation contract and the route list by month

tuition.causes: fewer children placed than budgeted, placements starting later, a placement paid from the circuit breaker fund instead, or a placement billed to a different tuition line
tuition.settles: the placement list by setting, with start dates and the tuition invoice for each

utilities.causes: weather, energy prices, or a bill for one year paid in another

conclusions.basis: `sources/data/munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13, report gf-school, every account put in one category by `CATEGORIES` in the generator.
conclusions.claim: $555,089 was left in three categories: building upkeep, counselors and teachers.
conclusions.detail: By category, net: building & grounds upkeep $195,934; counselors & psychologists $191,162; teachers & substitutes $167,992. Accounts under budget left $1,683,552 in all, and the surplus is what remained, $482,118. The ledger shows where money was left, never why.

c_three.unit: left over in the three largest categories

conclusions.not_shown: Why any category was left under budget — vacancies, placements, prices and restraint all produce the same ledger.
conclusions.so_what: Accounts over budget used $1,201,434; the largest overrun was paraprofessionals, $208,082 over.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2023 to FY2026 period 13, gf-school; the category table in the generator.
conclusions.claim: 59% of the surplus ($283,991) sat in discretionary lines thrift could explain.
conclusions.detail: Discretionary means supplies, upkeep and equipment — the split is ours, stated in the method table. 2 of the 3 discretionary categories were also left under budget in all 4 closed years held, which reads as budgeted high as much as run lean. It is the most thrift could explain, not a finding that it did.

c_disc_share.unit: of the surplus in discretionary lines

conclusions.not_shown: Whether anyone chose to spend less. That would show in the monthly journal, which is not published.
conclusions.so_what: The other $198,127 sat in staff, tuition and benefit lines, which follow vacancies, placements and prices.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13, salary lines (object 51xxxx) by category; School Committee minutes, 29 July 2026.
conclusions.claim: Salary lines left $192,211 net, though paraprofessionals ran $208,082 over.
conclusions.detail: Counselors & psychologists left $191,162 and teachers & substitutes $167,992. The 29 July 2026 minutes say money in a special-education teacher account "was associated with a leave of absence", and was moved to cover paraprofessional overages. Vacancies, leaves and hiring steps all fit the rest; the position-control roster would settle it.

s_net.unit: left over in salary lines, net

conclusions.not_shown: Which posts were vacant or on leave, and for how long. A dollar is not a post (rule 7, rule 11).
conclusions.so_what: The record names one leave of absence; no document here says why counselor money was left.

conclusions.basis: `sources/data/munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13, report gf-school, type E; `sources/data/munis-ledger.csv`, FY2026 period 12, department 300; joined account by account on org and object.
conclusions.claim: The FY26 school surplus stands at $482,118, $16.95 more than the June ledger showed.
conclusions.detail: The period-12 report run on 1 September 2026 allowed the year to close anywhere between $482,101 and $718,885. The period-13 report run on 6 October 2026 lands at the bottom of that range: the only change between them is $16.95 of a purchase order released in one supplies account.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether period 13 is complete: the report was run while purchase orders were still open.
conclusions.so_what: Not one of the 415 accounts changed its spending between the two runs.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 and FY2025 period 13, the encumbrances column, department 300.
conclusions.claim: $236,767 is still committed to open purchase orders, across 27 accounts.
conclusions.detail: The two largest are electricity charges ($62,362) and collaborative tuitions ($58,708). The FY2025 report of the same department, run the same day, shows $0 encumbered: that year is fully closed and this one is not.
conclusions.not_shown: Which orders will be paid, released, or carried into the next year.
conclusions.so_what: Paid, the surplus stays at $482,118; released, it can rise to at most $718,885.

conclusions.basis: School Committee minutes, 29 July 2026, pages 3 to 4; `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13.
conclusions.claim: In July the Committee heard FY26 would return well below FY25’s $600,000.
conclusions.detail: The minutes of 29 July 2026 record the business manager as "confident the remaining amount would be well below that figure" — the FY25 return, put at about 2.5% of the budget. As a share of FY26’s revised budget the floor is 1.8% and the ceiling 2.7%. Whether the statement holds depends on the open purchase orders.

stated.unit: returned in FY25, as stated in the minutes

conclusions.not_shown: What the business manager meant by "that figure", the dollars or the share; and a minute is a summary, not a transcript.
conclusions.so_what: The floor, $482,118, is below it; the ceiling, $718,885, is above it.

conclusions.basis: `munis-school-ytd.csv`, FY2026 period 13, available_budget and encumbrances grouped by the 4th segment of the account string.
conclusions.claim: Operations & maintenance holds $185,494 of the surplus and $106,098 of what is still open.
conclusions.detail: Of the operations & maintenance surplus, $11,352 is salary and $174,142 is not. The Town’s explanation for FY25’s surplus was unfilled facilities posts; nothing in this ledger says whether FY26 is the same story — it shows dollars by account, not posts.
conclusions.not_shown: Why any of it was left unspent. A dollar is not a post (rule 7, rule 11).
conclusions.so_what: Next largest: instruction, $112,278 unspent; out-of-district tuition, $58,708 still open.

grain: DOLLARS, department 300 (school general fund) only, FY2026 period 13 as run on 6 October 2026, 415 accounts — compared account by account with the period-12 run of 1 September 2026. Not a comparison of budget to actual: one ledger at two periods.
not_established: Why any category was left under budget. The ledger shows where money was left; vacancies, placements, prices and restraint all produce the same rows.
Whether anyone chose to spend less. The discretionary share is the most thrift could explain, not a finding that it did; the monthly journal would show it and is not published.
Whether the $236,767 still encumbered will be paid, released, or carried into FY2027.
Where the $85,090 moved into the department during the year came from — net per account, no counterparty.
What "expense accounts" meant in the 29 July 2026 minutes, and so whether the ledger agrees with "approximately 100.2% expended".
Why operations & maintenance was left unspent — dollars are not posts.
What was said under "FY26 Year End Budget review" on 2 September 2026 and 9 September 2026: no minutes for either meeting are held.
